prompt:
A full-body vertical 2:3 (1024×1536) character card image of an adult woman — the personification of the element Einsteinium (아인슈타이늄) itself — the sovereign of the Einsteinium Nation. A female character who IS the element; her costume, ornaments and colors carry the element’s traits. Both hands are ordinary human hands and hold nothing.

1. STYLE
A Japanese anime key visual with a painterly finish: an anime-style character with an elegant adult anime face, large expressive eyes, a small nose and mouth, fine coloured linework and soft cel-to-painted shading with painted highlights in the hair and fabric. Behind her, a richly painted background with layered painterly colour, subtle visible brushwork, atmospheric perspective and cinematic depth. Luminous, rich colours; crisp focal details on the face and costume, softer painted edges toward the distance.
Face proportions: a short midface and a soft, gently rounded jawline with a small soft chin; any crown or headpiece sits above her hairline. Her eyes keep the shape and size described below.

2. CHARACTER
Age: about twenty — a youthful face; no facial lines.
Face — her own: a cute, bright-eyed sweetness; warm beige skin; heart-shaped face; eyes on the larger side of natural — almond-shaped eyes of natural size, level outer eye corners; soft rounded brows; a nose with a soft, rounded tip, of natural size; softly full, heart-shaped lips of natural size; ice-blue eyes; rosy flushed cheeks.
Body and hair: petite and compact yet curvaceous — full bust and rounded hips on a small frame build; huge voluminous twin tails reaching past the knees with choppy uneven bangs; soft ash-white hair dusted with tiny specks glowing soft blue, like luminous falling ash.
Hair: her hair is worn exactly as described above — loose, long or cut as named; do not pin it up into a bun or tuck it under goggles or a hat unless the hair above is an updo.
Expression: one brow slightly raised, attentive eyes.
Her element, carried in her design: einsteinium: a soft silvery synthetic metal first found in the fallout of the first hydrogen-bomb test in late 1952 on a Pacific coral atoll, sifted from filter papers flown through the towering cloud and from scraps of the atoll's coral, born when uranium swallowed fifteen neutrons in a single instant; the find was kept secret for years, and she was named for the most famous physicist of the century, the genius of relativity; her best-known form glows a soft blue by its own radioactivity and is so fierce that it slowly shatters its own crystal structure, and only the tiniest amounts of her have ever been gathered.
Anatomy: one head, two arms and two legs, each joined at its natural joint; natural hands with five fingers.

3. COSTUME — STEAMPUNK
Costume: late-Victorian industrial dress — a high-necked blouse with a waistcoat or a tailored tail coat, leather gloves, a work apron or utility belt with brass fittings, goggles hung at the neck or a small instrument as ornament; below, a short bustle skirt and laced boots; the traits above as colour accents. No crown unless the opening line says she wears one; steam, pipes and gauges in the scene.
Silhouette: one large brass mechanical gauntlet covering a whole arm over an otherwise trim outfit — the contrast makes the shape. Only the overall shape is fixed; design the details freely in the element's materials and palette. This silhouette overrides the overall shape of the costume above.
Colours: fallout-ash white, self-glow soft blue, lagoon turquoise, pale coral pink.
Exposure (bold): her outfit opens to show skin — the neckline opened down to the sternum with natural cleavage, bare forearms, and bare legs above the boots or through a high slit where the silhouette allows; pieces stay symmetrical. Nothing slipped off. Intimate areas covered; no corset; keep the costume above, material and palette.

4. SCENE
World: around 1905, a patent office in an old clock-tower town: walls of wooden pigeonholes crammed with brass invention models, an ancient astronomical clock tower seen through the window with a tram rolling beneath it, and a clerk's desk where a young mind once dreamed of riding a beam of light.
Pose: standing confidently, her body turned slightly while her face looks toward the viewer.
Light: bright warm sunlight with soft sky light bounced from white clouds.
Composition: vertical 2:3 full-body framing with modest headroom and clear space below the boots — the whole figure from the top of her head or headpiece to both feet stays inside the frame, occupying about four-fifths of the image height, with the same camera distance in every world; her hands stay inside the frame. Camera level with her face with natural portrait perspective; her head level, chin neither raised nor tucked — no upward perspective on her face, no wide-angle distortion, no low angle, no close crop.

5. CONSTRAINTS
One figure only; no text or numbers except her element's own chemical symbol (Es) and atomic number (99) — and those only as part of the scene: engraved, embroidered or glowing on her costume, a banner, a sign or a machine, never as a floating label, corner badge, periodic-table tile, caption or overlay on the picture; no logo or watermark.
Avoid: flat single-tone cel shading, photographic appearance, semi-realistic face, plastic 3D-render finish, armor plates, cape, modern plastic, sci-fi.
